snippet: The way with no way: when grace has struck firm, one word from the teacher and the immersion is ever-risen — no means required. Four impossibilities: no nature to attain, nothing to notify, no covering to remove, no one
text: the way with no way when grace has struck firm one word from the teacher and the immersion is ever risen no means required four impossibilities no nature to attain nothing to notify no covering to remove no one to enter the means itself impossible all is one consciousness only reality unmeasured unbounded unfaded uncontrolled unindicated unelaborated autonomous bliss dense i am that with the universe mirrored in me no mantra worship meditation or conduct binds one who sees this steadily

snippet: Every use of means is void: nothing to attain, notify, unveil, or enter — all is Śiva already.

snippet: Here "yoga-limb" means one thing only: thinking it through. But what is there to think? The Lord, who is self-shining, is yourself. So what could a means do? It can't get you your nature — you have it eternally. It can't

snippet: And the means itself, as something separate from you, is equally impossible. So: all this is one reality, consciousness and nothing else — time can't measure it, place can't bound it, qualities can't fade it, shapes can'
